titulo: Think Before You Act! Grammar and Ethics in Medical Discoveries
titulo_es: Piensa antes de actuar: gramática y ética en los descubrimientos médicos
estandares: Ordeno hechos pasados distinguiendo cuál ocurrió primero. Doy instrucciones secuenciadas y argumento sobre dilemas éticos en el campo médico.
competencias: Diferenciar pasado simple y pasado perfecto; secuenciar procesos con imperativos y conectores de orden; comprender textos sobre avances médicos; expresar y escribir la hora con precisión.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes reconstruyen un caso real de la historia de la medicina: narran en orden qué había pasado antes y qué ocurrió después, y proponen un protocolo ético en imperativos numerados.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students reconstruct a real case from the history of medicine: they narrate in order what had happened before and what happened next, and propose an ethical protocol written as numbered imperatives.

lecciones.content_es:
El pasado antes del pasado

Se forma con had + participio, igual para todas las personas: She had finished the report before the meeting.

  • Negativo: hadn't — They hadn't arrived yet.
  • Pregunta: Had you seen it before?

Para qué sirve

Marca cuál de dos acciones pasadas ocurrió primero: When I got to the lab, the experiment had already started. (primero empezó el experimento)

Palabras que lo acompañan

already, just, never, before, by the time, after, when.

Ojo

Si el orden ya es evidente por los conectores before o after, muchos hablantes usan solo el pasado simple. El pasado perfecto se vuelve necesario cuando el orden no es obvio.
lecciones.content_en:
The past before the past

It is formed with had + participle, the same for every person: She had finished the report before the meeting.

  • Negative: hadn't — They hadn't arrived yet.
  • Question: Had you seen it before?

What it is for

It marks which of two past actions happened first: When I got to the lab, the experiment had already started.

Words that go with it

already, just, never, before, by the time, after, when.

Careful

If the order is already clear from before or after, many speakers use only the simple past. The past perfect becomes necessary when the order is not obvious.

lecciones.content_es:
La línea del tiempo

El pasado simple cuenta los hechos en orden; el pasado perfecto retrocede a algo anterior.

The nurse checked the chart. The patient had taken the medicine an hour before.

Cómo elegir

  • Si narras una secuencia normal, todo en pasado simple: He woke up, got dressed and left.
  • Si haces un salto atrás dentro de la narración, usa pasado perfecto: He was tired because he hadn't slept.

Con when

La diferencia cambia el sentido:

  • When I arrived, they started the meeting. → empezaron después de que llegué.
  • When I arrived, they had started the meeting. → ya había empezado.
lecciones.content_en:
The timeline

The past simple tells events in order; the past perfect steps back to something earlier.

The nurse checked the chart. The patient had taken the medicine an hour before.

How to choose

  • For a normal sequence, everything in the past simple: He woke up, got dressed and left.
  • For a jump back inside the narration, use the past perfect: He was tired because he hadn't slept.

With when

The difference changes the meaning:

  • When I arrived, they started the meeting. → they started after I arrived.
  • When I arrived, they had started the meeting. → it had already begun.

lecciones.content_es:
Instrucciones paso a paso

El imperativo usa el verbo en forma base, sin sujeto: Wash your hands. Wear gloves. Do not touch the sample.

Para instrucciones escritas y protocolos se prefiere do not completo en vez de don't.

Conectores de secuencia

First · Next · Then · After that · Meanwhile (mientras tanto) · Once (una vez que) · Finally.

First, sterilize the instruments. Next, prepare the sample. Finally, record the results.

Alternativas al imperativo

  • Formal y neutral: The sample must be refrigerated.
  • Con obligación: You have to sign the consent form.
  • Con sugerencia: It is advisable to…
lecciones.content_en:
Step-by-step instructions

The imperative uses the base verb, with no subject: Wash your hands. Wear gloves. Do not touch the sample.

In written instructions and protocols the full do not is preferred over don't.

Sequence connectors

First · Next · Then · After that · Meanwhile · Once · Finally.

First, sterilize the instruments. Next, prepare the sample. Finally, record the results.

Alternatives to the imperative

  • Formal and neutral: The sample must be refrigerated.
  • With obligation: You have to sign the consent form.
  • With a suggestion: It is advisable to…

fichas.d_en: In formal texts it is written in full, not don't.

lecciones.content_es:
El campo médico

treatment (tratamiento), cure, diagnosis (diagnóstico), symptom, disease (enfermedad), surgery (cirugía), transplant, therapy, drug (medicamento), dose, side effect (efecto secundario), patient, clinical trial (ensayo clínico).

Hitos históricos

the discovery of penicillin, the first heart transplant, the polio vaccine, the mapping of the human genome.

Verbos útiles

discover, develop, test, approve, prescribe, prevent, treat, heal, recover from.

Ojo

drug en contexto médico es medicamento; illness es la experiencia de estar enfermo y disease la enfermedad como entidad clínica. Sensible aquí no aplica: la palabra para «sensible al dolor» es sensitive.
lecciones.content_en:
The medical field

treatment, cure, diagnosis, symptom, disease, surgery, transplant, therapy, drug, dose, side effect, patient, clinical trial.

Historical milestones

the discovery of penicillin, the first heart transplant, the polio vaccine, the mapping of the human genome.

Useful verbs

discover, develop, test, approve, prescribe, prevent, treat, heal, recover from.

Careful

drug in a medical context means medicine; illness is the experience of being unwell and disease the clinical condition.

lecciones.content_es:
Conceptos clave

informed consent (consentimiento informado), confidentiality, privacy, autonomy, fairness (equidad), access to healthcare, malpractice (mala praxis), consequence, accountability (rendición de cuentas).

Argumentar en un dilema

  • Plantear: The question is whether…
  • A favor: One argument in favor is that… · The main benefit is…
  • En contra: On the other hand… · A serious concern is that… · This could lead to…
  • Concluir: All things considered, I believe…

Modales de obligación moral

Doctors must respect privacy. · Researchers should disclose risks. · Nobody ought to be tested without consent.
lecciones.content_en:
Key concepts

informed consent, confidentiality, privacy, autonomy, fairness, access to healthcare, malpractice, consequence, accountability.

Arguing in a dilemma

  • Framing: The question is whether…
  • In favor: One argument in favor is that… · The main benefit is…
  • Against: On the other hand… · A serious concern is that… · This could lead to…
  • Concluding: All things considered, I believe…

Modals of moral obligation

Doctors must respect privacy. · Researchers should disclose risks. · Nobody ought to be tested without consent.

lecciones.t_en: The time: saying it and writing it
lecciones.content_es:
Las dos formas

  • Conversacional: ten past three (3:10), quarter to eight (7:45), half past six (6:30)
  • Digital: three ten, seven forty-five, six thirty

Reloj de 12 y de 24 horas

En contextos médicos y aeronáuticos se usa el de 24 horas: 14:30 = fourteen thirty. En la vida diaria, el de 12 con a.m. y p.m.

Momentos especiales

noon (12:00), midnight (00:00), sharp (en punto exacto): at 9 o'clock sharp.

Preposiciones y duración

  • at + hora exacta · from … to … · until · by (a más tardar)
  • The shift runs from 7 to 3. · Be there by 8.
  • Duración: It takes two hours. It lasts 45 minutes.
lecciones.content_en:
The two forms

  • Conversational: ten past three (3:10), quarter to eight (7:45), half past six (6:30)
  • Digital: three ten, seven forty-five, six thirty

12- and 24-hour clock

In medical and aviation contexts the 24-hour clock is used: 14:30 = fourteen thirty. In everyday life, the 12-hour clock with a.m. and p.m.

Special moments

noon (12:00), midnight (00:00), sharp (exactly): at 9 o'clock sharp.

Prepositions and duration

  • at + exact time · from … to … · until · by (no later than)
  • The shift runs from 7 to 3. · Be there by 8.
  • Duration: It takes two hours. It lasts 45 minutes.

fichas.d_en: Exactly on the hour: at 9 o'clock sharp.

fichas.d_en: No later than 8, not exactly at 8.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El periodo se apoya en el orden de los hechos. El pasado perfecto (had + participio) retrocede a lo que ocurrió primero; el pasado simple narra la secuencia. Y para explicar un procedimiento se usan imperativos con conectores de orden.

Puntos gramaticales

  • had + participio, igual para todas las personas.
  • When + pasado simple vs when + pasado perfecto cambian el orden de los hechos.
  • Imperativo: verbo base; en protocolos formales, do not completo.
  • Secuencia: First, Next, Then, After that, Meanwhile, Once, Finally.

Vocabulario

Léxico médico (treatment, diagnosis, side effect, clinical trial), ética (informed consent, confidentiality, accountability) y la hora con at, by, until, take y last.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The term rests on the order of events. The past perfect (had + participle) steps back to what happened first; the past simple tells the sequence. And to explain a procedure you use imperatives with sequence connectors.

Grammar points

  • had + participle, the same for every person.
  • When + past simple vs when + past perfect change the order of the events.
  • Imperative: base verb; in formal protocols, the full do not.
  • Sequence: First, Next, Then, After that, Meanwhile, Once, Finally.

Vocabulary

Medical vocabulary (treatment, diagnosis, side effect, clinical trial), ethics (informed consent, confidentiality, accountability) and the time with at, by, until, take and last.
